parts.text: The first reference photo sets the sculpting style, clay finish, lighting and camera framing. The second reference photo is the character: keep the exact same face sculpt and head proportions. Change only what this description says: Photograph of a hand-sculpted stop-motion claymation figure, matte plasticine with fingerprints, tool marks and pressed texture, soft studio lighting, highly detailed, in exactly the style of the reference photos. A grotesque disfigured clay WOMAN (female, not the man in the reference: copy only the reference's clay style, pose and framing) with an oversized bobble head, mottled skin, small sunken bloodshot eyes in swollen red-rimmed lids, a thin neck and narrow hunched shoulders, head turned three-quarters toward the viewer's right. Ashen grey-white clay skin, short glossy black finger-waved curls under an enormous wide-brimmed black mourning hat with a torn black lace veil. No mask: a towering elegant woman's face with high sharp cheekbones, heavy dark eye makeup, cruel narrowed eyes and a wide wicked smile of glossy blood-red lips. Wearing an elegant fitted white gown with a low sweetheart neckline showing some cleavage, puffed shoulders, black lace trim and a black silk rose at the waist, a few spatters of blood, a tight choker of dark blood-red garnets, BOTH of her hands are raised in front of her chest, fingers spread like claws, every fingertip on both hands ending in a long curved blackened-steel blade nail as long as a forearm, all ten blade nails fanned out toward the viewer, blood on the tips. A dark carved-wood gothic castle hall lit by tall dripping candles in iron sconces, sculpted as a miniature claymation diorama in matte plasticine, softly out of focus behind her, no signs or lettering. FACING: exactly like the first reference photo, her body is in three-quarter view and her head and face are turned about 45 degrees toward the RIGHT side of the image (the viewer's right), nose pointing right; never turned to the left side and never straight on. Three-quarter view from the hips up, whole head, mask and weapons inside the frame with a little space above the head, figure centred, square 1:1 composition. SCALE (the same for every figure in the series): the figure is the same size in the frame as in the first reference photo, the bobble head the same size relative to the body, and weapons true to scale with the hands, never oversized or tiny. Both hands are raised and fully visible inside the frame, all ten blade nails spread; neither hand hangs down or is hidden. Avoid: text, logo, letters, watermark, brand marks, sports team logo, red chevrons or triangles on the mask, full-face goalie mask covering the forehead and eyes, white screaming ghost mask, black hooded robe, pins in a grid, extra fingers, deformed hands, cropped head, photo of a real person, cartoon outline, flat 2D, face turned to the left, mirrored pose, red and green striped sweater, brown fedora

The first reference photo sets the sculpting style, clay finish, lighting and camera framing. The second reference photo is the character: keep the exact same face sculpt and head proportions. Change only what this description says: Photograph of a hand-sculpted stop-motion claymation figure, matte plasticine with fingerprints, tool marks and pressed texture, soft studio lighting, highly detailed, in exactly the style of the reference photos. A small evil child's toy doll come to life, a burned killer doll with a big round doll head, short stubby limbs and plastic doll hands, head turned three-quarters toward the viewer's right. Blistered charred black plastic skin, crusted and cracked by fire, with glimpses of pale melted vinyl underneath, a few singed sooty black yarn hair tufts stuck to the scalp. No mask: a melted burned doll face, one huge bulging cracked glass doll eye staring out, the other eye socket a burnt hollow, a lipless stitched grin of tiny white doll teeth. Wearing tiny tattered mustard-brown corduroy dungarees with a bib pocket and frayed patches, scorched black at the edges, over a sooty little turtleneck, his right fist grips a big bloody kitchen knife. The inside of a giant child's dollhouse: pastel flowered wallpaper streaked with soot and scorch marks, toy blocks, a tiny rocking horse and a broken toy chair, sculpted as a miniature claymation diorama in matte plasticine, softly out of focus behind him, no signs or lettering. FACING: exactly like the first reference photo, his body is in three-quarter view and his head and face are turned about 45 degrees toward the RIGHT side of the image (the viewer's right), nose pointing right; never turned to the left side and never straight on. Three-quarter view from the hips up, whole head, mask and weapons inside the frame with a little space above the head, figure centred, square 1:1 composition. SCALE (the same for every figure in the series): the figure is the same size in the frame as in the first reference photo, the bobble head the same size relative to the body, and weapons true to scale with the hands, never oversized or tiny. His right hand grips the held weapon in a tight clenched fist seen from the back of the hand, knuckles toward the camera, palm hidden, the blade angled up and out; his other hand hangs open. Avoid: text, logo, letters, watermark, brand marks, sports team logo, red chevrons or triangles on the mask, full-face goalie mask covering the forehead and eyes, white screaming ghost mask, black hooded robe, pins in a grid, extra fingers, deformed hands, cropped head, photo of a real person, cartoon outline, flat 2D, face turned to the left, mirrored pose, long finger blades, clawed glove with four long knives, red and green striped sweater, brown fedora
